title: 2001 AMC 10 Problem 6
statement: Let \(P(n)\) and \(S(n)\) denote the product and the sum, respectively, of the digits of the integer \(n.\) For example, \(P(23)=6\) and \(S(23)=5.\) Suppose \(N\) is a two-digit number such that \(N=P(N)+S(N).\) What is the units digit of \(N?\)

solutions.text:
Write \(N=10a+b.\) Then \(P(N)=ab\) and \(S(N)=a+b,\) so \(10a+b=ab+a+b.\) This reduces to \(9a=ab,\) and since \(a\ne0,\) we get \(b=9.\)

The units digit is \(9.\) Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write \(N=10a+b,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are its digits
